CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the ongoing management of anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms, with a focus on recent treatment adjustments and their impact on Mr. Smith's overall well-being.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith presents for his follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed response to his current treatment regimen. He notes that while his sleep duration has remained consistent at approximately 7 hours per night, he continues to experience nighttime awakenings, particularly around 3 AM. He describes the morning grogginess as persistent, which he attributes to the combination of trazodone and melatonin. Mr. Smith expresses concern regarding the potential impact of this grogginess on his daily functioning.
In terms of fatigue, Mr. Smith states that he has noticed a slight decline in energy levels over the past week, particularly following stressful days at work. He reports that his headaches have fluctuated, with an increase in frequency to 3-4 episodes per week, although he maintains that their intensity remains moderate, typically rated between 4-6 out of 10. He continues to utilize ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief, which has been effective, with no gastrointestinal complaints.
Mr. Smith acknowledges that while cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) has been beneficial, he is struggling to maintain consistency with mindfulness practices due to increased workload and stress. He has continued his yoga sessions but has had to reduce his acupuncture treatments due to scheduling conflicts.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (stable usage) 6. Amitriptyline 40 mg nightly 7. Topiramate 50 mg daily 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued dosage)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, where he finds the work environment increasingly demanding. He reports that while he remains committed to his running group, recent project deadlines have limited his ability to participate regularly. He maintains a balanced diet, abstains from alcohol, and is attempting to limit caffeine to improve sleep quality.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Sleep quality remains an issue; anxiety is manageable; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency has increased; intensity remains moderate; no visual disturbances or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 74 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, appears slightly fatigued compared to previous visit. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable but somewhat anxious.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Lorazepam remains at 1 mg as needed, with a discussion regarding the importance of consistent CBT attendance and mindfulness practice to further manage anxiety symptoms. 2. Insomnia: Consider reducing trazodone to 50 mg at bedtime to alleviate morning grogginess while monitoring sleep quality. Continue melatonin at 10 mg. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Increase amitriptyline to 50 mg nightly and maintain topiramate at 50 mg daily to address the increased headache frequency. Schedule follow-up in one month to reassess headache management. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage Mr. Smith to prioritize physical activity and mindfulness practices, and consider a referral to a sleep specialist if fatigue does not improve with the adjusted treatment plan.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2029-04-01 to monitor symptoms, evaluate treatment efficacy, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is encouraged to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
